Three paths outside FILES are modified: `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs`, `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_integrated_runs.mjs`, and `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proposed_patch.mjs`. Each edit is forced by the engine change and none is sibling-owned — the pre-review pass doubles the `driver:proof-run` count and moves red-`Run:` handling out of the review fix loop (proof_runs, integrated_runs), and `actor` joining `REVIEWER_SCHEMA.required` breaks proposed_patch's whole-array `deepEqual`. The adaptations are disclosed in comments and each keeps the assertion the file exists to make (proposed_patch now pins `required.indexOf('proposedPatch') === -1` alongside the new array). Recording the footprint overrun, not asking for a change.; `skills/ultrapowers/references/report-format.md`'s new `integratedChecks` row says "`[]` when the run declared no checks and when no tree was adopted", but the engine's loop sits inside the per-wave `if (merge.status === 'MERGED')` block (fleet/run-engine.mjs, after the integrated-`Run:` loop), so a multi-wave run appends every command once per adopted wave. Unlike the `driver:integrated-check` event, the record shape the plan fixes (`{ cmd, exit, stdout, minor }`) carries no `wave`, so a reader sees repeated `cmd` values with no way to attribute them. Faithful to M4 — worth one clause in the row, e.g. "one item per command per adopted wave, in wave order; the matching `driver:integrated-check` event carries the wave number". The `integratedRuns` row above has the same silence, so this is a consistency gap rather than a regression.; Three paths modified outside FILES (none sibling-owned, and each a direct consequence of the change rather than scope creep — named per the footprint rule): `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs` (dispatch order, event counts and iters shift because the pre-review pass runs `Run:` commands at iter 0, and two legs now assert `fix:T1:0` / `reviewVerdict: 'proof-red'` / `proofFixes: 1`), `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_integrated_runs.mjs` (a `driver:proof-run` count 2 → 4 plus an `iter === 1` count), and `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proposed_patch.mjs` (`deepEqual(item.required, ['severity','detail','actor'])` after the schema change, plus a retained assertion that `proposedPatch` is never required). No action needed beyond recording the wider footprint.; Doubled prefix in task notes: the actor-routing block builds `planNotes = planDefects.filter(…).map((p) => 'plan-defect: ' + p.detail)`, but a reviewer-supplied detail routed by the textual path already begins with `plan-defect:` (that prefix is what the router matches on), so the note reads `plan-defect: plan-defect: M2 cannot hold as written`. The spec literal `plan-defect: <detail>` is still satisfied and nothing downstream parses it, so this is cosmetic; strip an existing prefix before prepending, e.g. `'plan-defect: ' + p.detail.replace(/^plan-defect:\s*/, '')`.; report-format.md's `tasks[].reviewVerdict` row still glosses `blocked-after-fix` as "implementer blocked during the fix round", but the pre-review pass adds a second producer of that verdict: fleet/run-engine.mjs returns `reviewVerdict: 'blocked-after-fix'` with `fixIterations: 0, proofFixes: 1` when the `fix:<id>:0` agent comes back BLOCKED/NEEDS_CONTEXT. Before this change `blocked-after-fix` implied `fixIterations: 1`, so a consumer reading the pair now sees a combination the reference does not describe. M9 only requires the `proof-red` addition, so this is advisory — one clause in the same row, e.g. "...blocked during a fix round, including the driver's pre-review repair round (`fixIterations: 0` with `proofFixes: 1`)". Same row, no rewrite of the pinned `proposedPatches` or `deferredVerification` text.; `checkEvidenceBlock` and `integratedCheckEvidenceBlock` (fleet/run-engine.mjs, the two new exports) differ only in their opening sentence; the per-command renderer `checks.map((c) => '

$ ' + c.cmd + '
exit ' + c.exit + (c.minor ? ' (minor)' : '') + '
' + c.stdout).join('')` is copy-pasted verbatim between them. The new sim does loop both functions over the same `sample` with the same expectations, so a divergence would be caught — which is why this is advisory and not blocking. Lifting the map into one `const checkLines = (checks) => ...` used by both would leave the opener as the only difference, matching how the pair is described in M3/M4 ("the same per-command lines"). Noted as house-keeping: the file's existing `runEvidenceBlock`/`integratedRunEvidenceBlock` pair duplicates the same way, so this follows the surrounding idiom rather than departing from it.; concern: out-of-FILES: fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs — M1 changes WHEN the Run: commands execute, so this pre-existing file's pins went red for the right reason (a green task now records two executions before review 1, and an always-red command ends at proof-red without a reviewer instead of looping to fix-loop-exhausted). fleet/roles/reviewer.md — the new `unverified:` paragraph says the finding "belongs among the findings, where the operator and the editor both read it", but the editor (critic) does not read it. At BASE the only reviewer→critic channel is the CANNOT-VERIFY checklist built at fleet/run-engine.mjs:1544-1557, and sibling task 1's M6 deletes that channel entirely; the critic prompt (fleet/run-engine.mjs:1554-1566) carries roles.critic, the plan path, the global constraints, the task list, the contracts block, blocked waves, the suite line and the integrated run evidence — no per-task minor findings. Minors reach the operator only, via the task row's `notes` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:891). Suggest dropping the editor from that clause, e.g. "It belongs among the findings, where the operator reads it, and grading it `minor` is what keeps it from stopping a merge it could not judge." M2 is satisfied either way (`cannot settle`, `minor`, `unverified:` all stay in the paragraph), so this is prose accuracy only.; fleet/roles/reviewer.md — rule 1 still ends "A requirement with no evidence is blocking", which now sits next to the new paragraph telling the referee that a requirement the diff cannot settle is a `minor` finding. Before this change the two were kept apart by the separate `cannotVerify` channel; now both land in `issues` and are distinguished only by severity, so a referee can read rule 1 as blocking exactly the case the new paragraph calls minor. Worth one clause in rule 1 naming the split — e.g. "A requirement the diff should carry and does not is blocking; a requirement the diff cannot settle at all is the `unverified:` case below." The file is inside FILES and no Proof `Run:` constrains rule 1's wording.; fleet/tests/test_roles_peer.mjs — deleting leg (e) (`IMPLEMENTER_SENTENCE`) leaves fleet/roles/implementer.md:30 with no pin anywhere in the tree; the only other mention of that rule is prose in CLAUDE.md:154, which pins nothing. M11 forbids the constant, not the coverage: a loose pin in the same spirit as the surviving REVIEWER_RULE_PATTERNS regexes — e.g. `assert.ok(/prefixed `exam:`/.test(read('implementer.md')), 'implementer.md no longer tells the implementer what a peer-written exam is')` — would keep #553 item 4 held while staying on the right side of the #612 call (register sweeps and clause pins stay, verbatim sentence legs go). Legs (b) and (d) lose nothing similarly: their subjects are still pinned by the surviving regexes and by fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proposed_patch.mjs.

awk 'BEGIN{RS=""} /how the work was produced/ && /is not a finding/ {f=1} END{exit !f}' fleet/roles/reviewer.md

awk 'BEGIN{RS=""} /CHECK EVIDENCE/ && /fix loop/ && /\(minor\)/ && /blocks nothing/ {f=1} END{exit !f}' fleet/roles/reviewer.md

! grep -qi 'cannot-verify' fleet/roles/critic.md && ! grep -qi 'checklist' fleet/roles/critic.md && ! grep -q 'Interfaces:' fleet/roles/critic.md && test "$(grep -c '^1\. ' fleet/roles/critic.md && awk 'BEGIN{RS=""} /INTEGRATED RUN EVIDENCE/ && /authoritative/ && /re-execution/ && /settled/ && /not a .deferredVerification/ && /human judgment/ && /not for a command the driver ran/ {f=1} END{exit !f}' fleet/roles/critic.md && grep -q 'INTEGRATED CHECK EVIDENCE' fleet/roles/critic.md && grep -q 'browser, runtime, external, manual' fleet/roles/critic.md

awk 'BEGIN{RS=""} /referee/ && /Run:/ && /Check:/ && /exit non-zero/ {f=1} END{exit !f}' fleet/roles/fix.md && ! grep -q 'question for the editor' fleet/roles/README.md && grep -q 'unverified:' fleet/roles/README.md

! grep -nE '\b(NEVER|ALWAYS|MUST)\b' fleet/roles/reviewer.md fleet/roles/critic.md fleet/roles/fix.md fleet/roles/README.md && ! grep -qi 'adversarial' fleet/roles/reviewer.md fleet/roles/critic.md fleet/roles/fix.md fleet/roles/README.md

! grep -q 'REFEREE_SENTENCES' fleet/tests/test_roles_peer.mjs && ! grep -q 'FIX_SENTENCE' fleet/tests/test_roles_peer.mjs && ! grep -q 'IMPLEMENTER_SENTENCE' fleet/tests/test_roles_peer.mjs && grep -q 'unverified:' fleet/tests/test_roles_peer.mjs && ! grep -q 'cannotVerify' fleet/tests/test_run_engine.mjs && ! grep -q 'sha256' fleet/tests/test_exam_edited_patches.mjs && node fleet/tests/test_roles_peer.mjs | grep -q 'ALL TESTS PASSED' && node fleet/tests/test_run_engine.mjs | grep -q 'ALL TESTS PASSED' && node fleet/tests/test_run_engine_critic_inputs.mjs | grep -q 'ALL TESTS PASSED' && node fleet/tests/test_exam_edited_patches.mjs | grep -q 'ALL TESTS PASSED' && python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_roles_run_evidence.py
